text:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — proposing we deprecate the legacy top_k:int parameter and replace it with a structured selection.policy object. sketch below, looking for concerns about shimming, cache churn, and telemetry.

devon: +1 on structured policy for long term. question: do we map top_k -> {type: "top_k", k: N} at the API edge? that seems simplest for compat.

sam: mapping at the edge is easiest for callers but will change request fingerprints (cache + batching keys). we should probably include a stable compatibility key to preserve caching.

anya: agree with sam. also need to consider evals: existing prompt sets assume top_k semantics. new policy object could allow other selection rules that change outputs.

maria: proposed shim behavior: if request contains top_k (int) and no selection.policy, mutate payload to add selection.policy = {"type":"top_k","k":<top_k>} and add header X-RW-Compat: top_k-bridge. no other mutation. minimal.

sam: ok but two tradeoffs: 1) cache keys: if we include full selection.policy in cache key, old requests become cache misses after migration. 2) batching: continuous-batch signatures need stable shape.

devon: for cache we can normalize policy into a canonical string and then include a compatibility token in the key when the bridge header exists. mapping: cache_key = base_key + (bridge ? ":compat:top_k" : ":policy:" + canonical_policy). that keeps old clients hitting the same cache.

maria: good idea. that avoids invalidating large serving caches. any perf impact?

anya: the extra header and canonicalization cost is tiny. main risk is accidentally masking clients that intentionally switch to new semantics — they'd still get old-path caching unless they opt-in.

devon: plan: 1) implement bridge shim with header. 2) enable shim by default but add opt-in header X-RW-Selection-Mode: new to opt into the structured path. 3) after N months, flip default and keep bridge available behind a tenant flag for legacy accounts.

sam: timeline: canary 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 2 weeks each. Telemetry we need: selection_policy_present, selection_mapped, cache_hit_by_compat_token, batch_signature_changes, median_latency_by_path.

maria: add metrics for integrity: selection_output_drift (compare outputs for mapped top_k vs explicit policy when both provided in canaries). will run evals to ensure behaviour parity.

anya: question about SDKs: should we ship client-side helpers that translate top_k to policy? probably yes — that reduces server-side burden later.

devon: agree. devex will prepare patches for JS/Python. but server shim still required for apps that can't upgrade quickly.

sam: small nit: document default behavior in API spec: if both top_k and selection.policy present, selection.policy wins and top_k is ignored with a warning header. Also emit a deprecation warning in the response body when top_k used.

maria: sounds good. also add a migration telemetry event that lists tenants still using top_k so PM can drive outreach.

deploy-bot: Deploy staged: compat-bridge v1 -> canary cluster. CI: green. Scheduled 2025-10-22 02:00 UTC. :rocket:

devon: safe roll: ensure we run a canary test suite that includes cache-hit regression checks and a small set of prompts used by top customers.

anya: I'll own the eval harness and quality checks. sam can own cache/key changes and rollout gating. maria will own the RFC updates and deprecation announcement draft.

maria: thanks all — I'll push the RFC follow-up doc and add the rollout checklist. will paste PR link when ready. :memo:
